phone_note: Discovery flagged (732) 664-3160 as low-confidence (NJ area code, not confirmed in a primary business source). Re-verification attempted: Booksy JSON-LD telephone field is null/absent; Instagram web_profile_info endpoint returned HTTP 400 (blocked, both desktop and mobile UA, with and without x-ig-app-id header) so the IG bio could not be checked directly; no dedicated Facebook business page was found for this exact business (only an unrelated 'Hair, Lash and Brow Boca' page). A third-party aggregator (LashLookup.com) lists (732) 664-3160, and two client-uploaded Booksy review-photo screenshots (iMessage conversations with a contact saved as 'Liv', phone header showing +1 (732) 664-3160) corroborate the same number, but neither of those is a source PUBLISHED BY THE BUSINESS ITSELF (bio/Booksy/Facebook About), so per the hard rule the number is omitted from the site and JSON-LD (recorded here as null with this note for the record, not fabricated).

brand_vibe: Warm, minimal, quiet-luxury: cream/beige textured logo card with cursive 'beleza' wordmark, a warm neutral cream-and-white lounge interior (cream armchairs, olive plant, candle), and an elegant black-and-white owner portrait. No pink/floral branding despite the lash-studio niche. Used the light-v2 skeleton (same niche structurally: lash studio) but replaced its plum-pink palette with a warm cream/espresso/mocha-gold palette matching DESIGN.md's 'amani' tokens (bg #f5f0e8 cream, ink #32281f espresso, accent-deep #8a6f4d mocha/gold-olive, accent-mid #a8907a taupe, accent-soft #ece1d0), with near-black espresso gradients (#241c12 to #18120b) for the dark CTA/footer bands instead of the exemplar's wine/plum. Full old-to-new hex/rgba palette mapping applied via global replace in the build script; merktop-badge gold (#D4A84B family) was left untouched.

images.curation_note: Booksy's own gallery for this business (11 photos initially downloaded) was almost entirely unusable per the visual curation rule: 4 were iPhone screenshots of a client dispute text conversation (rejected: captions/UI chrome + negative content), 1 was a generic purple Booksy staff-avatar placeholder, 1 was a personal bikini/pool photo (not treatment-related), 1 was a personal fashion portrait on stairs (not treatment-related, not usable as gallery), and 1 was a 100x100px thumbnail (too low-res). Per the pipeline's IG-rescue rule (fewer than 5 usable photos), Instagram rescue was attempted (profile page + individual post page) but blocked (HTTP 400 / empty shell). Rescue instead came from Booksy's own resource_photos/review_photos CDN paths (found by re-scanning the raw Booksy HTML for cloudfront URLs beyond the biz_photo pattern) and from Google Maps business photos surfaced via a third-party directory (LashLookup) that exposes lh3.googleusercontent.com URLs for this exact listing. Of those additional finds: 1 close-up (mascara wand mid-application, POV process shot) was rejected as not a finished result; 1 was a broken/placeholder Google image; 1 had a visible photographer watermark ('Julia Sylvester', also not verifiably this salon's own client); 1 showed a surgical mask covering the lower face (rejected per the established precedent). Net result: only 3 genuinely usable real photos were found (1 lounge interior, 2 finished lash+brow close-ups) plus 1 usable owner portrait and 1 logo card. Per PIPELINE.md's explicit rule ('si quedan menos de 5 buenas, mejor menos secciones con buenas fotos que rellenar con malas'), the gallery section was shrunk from the template's default 6 tiles to 1 real photo tile + 1 'follow on Instagram for more' CTA card, and one of the two close-ups (hero-1.jpg) is shown twice at different crops (portrait 3:4 in the hero, wide 4:5 in the gallery) rather than padding with a 4th weak or duplicate-feeling image.

research_note: Research completed 2026-07-20. Primary source: python3 scripts/booksy_dossier.py against the Booksy business page (id 1014600), which returned JSON-LD-confirmed name, address, rating (4.9), review count (63), the full 18-service menu with prices/durations, and 10 verbatim reviews, matching every figure already confirmed by discovery. Own-website check: 4 domain variants tried, none resolve. Phone: could not be confirmed in a business-published source (Booksy field is null, IG bio blocked, no dedicated Facebook page); the discovery-flagged (732) 664-3160 is corroborated only by a third-party directory and by customer-uploaded review-photo screenshots, neither of which counts as a primary business source per the hard rule, so it is omitted (null) everywhere on the site and in JSON-LD. Email: carried forward from discovery as already confirmed; could not be independently re-located in the static Booksy HTML or IG bio (both attempts blocked/inconclusive) but is consistently and exclusively tied to this business across every search result, with no conflicting address found; used only in the outreach draft, not surfaced on the public demo page.
